label: Actual-root favourings are good-general, from nonlimitation and one favouring
description: Fix an actual root r at w and a favouring determination favours phi of r. By excluded middle, phi is good-general or not. Suppose not. Any admissible profile containing r's actual profile and the good-generality token is realized by one favouring psi; favours phi is in it, so phi = psi, and the token makes psi good-general, a contradiction. So r's admissible actual profile (root-profile admissibility) excludes good-generality, which is pure and, by pure admissibility, admissible somewhere. The structural L bridge (a bearer whose admissible profile excludes an admissible pure determination has a represented limiting principle; its distinct simply prior being is the shared CausalityFrame's PriorSimply, PRIOR_1) gives r a limiting principle, which actual roots lack. No premise mentions an absence or its explanation: the excluding determination is the favouring itself, so the #2153 E premise (no unexplained absence at roots) is not used. The main theorem uses no axioms. The Comparator companion favouringControls (three Mathlib axioms; the #2153 two-being carrier with the Lane 2b profiles) gives a positive witness and, for each non-logical premise, a row where it fails, the others hold and a root with the D-directed favouring fails the conclusion; two rows for L show which of its inputs fails when the D-directed favouring is counted impure (RootPurity) or pure (joint compossibility). The assignments say nothing about what favouring, purity or admissibility metaphysically are.
